summary: Sidecar proxy header truncation leads to duplicate tool invocations on retry
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated duplicate side-effects (external webhook POSTs, DB writes) when using Redwood SDKs behind a local sidecar/proxy that performs header normalization. The symptoms occur after transient network interruptions when the client SDK retries a streaming/function-call request.

Impact:
- Production customer (QuanticaHealth, Dedicated) experiencing duplicate patient-notification webhook deliveries and duplicate ingestion rows.
- Seen across Python and Go SDKs; TS SDK reproduction confirmed in-house by Support.
- Intermittent but repeatable when client path includes the customer's Envoy-based sidecar.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: prod us-east-1, pinned model open/llama-2-13b-redwood-quantized v2.1.
- Customer runs a sidecar (Envoy 1.27) that rewrites/sanitizes headers and enforces 64-char header length limits.
- SDKs used: python 1.8.2, go 0.6.4, ts 2.1.0.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start an interactive streaming function-call session that triggers an external webhook on tool confirmation (confirmed webhook target: https://webhooks.quantica.health/notify).
2) During a long response (2000+ tokens), force a transient connection cut (e.g., drop packets / restart sidecar).
3) Client SDK automatically performs a retry/resume according to default resume policy.
4) Observe two POSTs to webhook target within ~6s of each other and two DB rows created by webhook consumer.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate downstream side-effects (webhook POSTs & DB inserts).
- Redwood server logs show original request received with Idempotency header (X-Redwood-Idempotency: 0b3f9d4a-...-long-token-128chars) but retry arrives with a truncated header (X-Redwood-Idempotency: 0b3f9d4a-...-truncated-64chars) due to sidecar limitation. The platform treats them as different idempotency tokens -> duplicates.

Expected behavior:
- Retries/resumes should preserve idempotency identity and the server should deduplicate tool invocations for the same logical request/session even when a proxy truncates or normalizes headers.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer's sidecar is silently truncating long idempotency tokens to 64 characters which causes token mismatch between original and retry. The server's idempotency dedup key is the exact header value, so truncated retries miss dedup records.
- SDK and server currently rely on header-preservation; no secondary fingerprint is computed for dedup.

Temporary mitigation suggested to customer:
- Reduce idempotency key length in SDK by configuring shorter idempotency tokens (workaround).
- Configure sidecar to pass-through headers without truncation or increase header length limits.
- As an immediate stopgap, switch to a request-scoped confirmation pattern on the tool consumer that deduplicates based on request_id embedded in the webhook payload.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Reproduced in-house by Support team with a local Envoy sidecar configured to trim headers >64 chars; observed token truncation and duplicate tool calls.
Checked server dedup index TTL and found dedup entries persisted for 10 minutes (expected); first request should have been visible to dedup on retry window.
Verified server logs do not normalize idempotency header beyond exact string match; dedup key uses header raw value and session_id fingerprinting is not enabled for function calls.
Customer confirmed they run Envoy with header_buffer_size config that enforces 64-character limit for some internal reasons (legacy policy).
SRE noted potential mitigation: compute secondary dedup fingerprint on server: SHA256(idempotency_header) truncated / normalized or include request_id from streaming resume handshake as dedup anchor.
Created engineering spike task to evaluate tolerant dedup (normalize/truncate-aware) and alternate anchoring (session_id + nonce) — PR drafted: platform#3214.
Risk: changing dedup matching rules could affect existing customers that rely on strict header semantics. Backward compatibility plan required.
comments: 2026-03-10 16:00 - Aisha Bennett (Support): Confirmed initial report with customer logs and asked for sidecar config snippet and header policy. Requested webhook timestamps and example request bodies.
2026-03-10 18:14 - QuanticaHealth (Customer): Sent sidecar envoy config and sample request/response pairs. Confirmed duplicate webhook deliveries observed between 15:32:11 and 15:32:17 UTC.

2026-03-11 09:27 - Diego Morales (Support): Reproduced locally with Envoy trimming; added reproduction notes and escalated to SRE/Serving Runtime with logs attached. Linked INT-4122 for deeper runtime investigation.

2026-03-11 14:45 - SRE (Rina Patel): Looked at dedup index and confirmed key equality is string exact match. Suggested interim recommendation to customer to shorten tokens or allow header passthrough; raised engineering task to evaluate server-side tolerant matching (spike #3214).

2026-03-12 11:05 - Engineering (Jon Kwon): Drafted PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3214 that computes secondary fingerprint (sha256 of header canonicalized) and falls back to session_id+nonce when idempotency header length differs. Marked as experimental feature gate.

2026-03-12 16:20 - Support (Diego Morales): Shared experimental mitigation plan with customer: enable experimental tolerant-dedup feature on their Dedicated instance behind a feature flag for two-week trial before GA. Customer requested SLA-safe mitigation plan and rollback steps.
resolution: Workaround provided: customer temporarily configured sidecar to preserve headers and increased header buffer to 256 chars; also shortened SDK-generated idempotency tokens in their integration. Engineering created spike and PR #3214 to add tolerant dedup matching using a normalized sha256 fingerprint and session_id anchoring. Next steps: QA the feature gate in staging, run canary on a small subset of Dedicated customers, and produce migration guidance. Ticket will be updated with rollout schedule post QA.
